header .subtitle: Every new page and notable improvement to UX Guidelines, newest first.
.rl-notes li: A Release Log page, linked from the footer, and the RSS feed in all six languages.
The home page now lists 70 references, and item titles are slightly bolder.
Ten new entries in People, from Herbert A. Simon to Harry Brignull.
An Other group on the home page for references that aren’t about a kind of page.
Every footer now carries the copyright line.
Copy any illustration as a PNG image, not just as SVG.
Phones use one consistent side margin, with tighter spacing around card groups.
Home page illustrations assemble as you scroll.
Placeholders stand in while a translation loads, and every font size sits on one type scale.
A not-found page that matches the rest of the site.
Accessibility: visible focus rings, search results you can move through by keyboard, and closed panels hidden from screen readers.
A sticky bar on phones keeps the page title, bookmark, and share in reach.
When to Use and How to Use sections on every reference page.
Portraits of the people behind the laws, and an RSS feed of new pages.
A fact check corrected 24 pages, People, and the Glossary in all six languages.
Search opens as a full-width results sheet, and bookmarks open in a sheet with a count and Clear all.
On phones, theme and language become two dropdowns side by side.
Search on phones drops in as a second row instead of hiding the top bar.
French, German, and Spanish pages get web addresses in their own language.
A Help panel with keyboard shortcuts: press ? for help and / to search.
Universal Icons illustrations now use real Lucide icons.
An accuracy audit applied 21 corrections across pages, People, and By Year.
Related links rechecked so that every one is on topic.
Section pills jump between home page groups, and a back-to-top button appears on every page.
Layouts tuned for tablets and phones.
Page Type groups get screen illustrations, and a Chat group for conversational pages and side panels.
A navy blue theme joins the theme options.
Copy any illustration as SVG from the button that appears on hover.
Page Type and Task Type tabs on the home page, with each reference in exactly one Page Type group.
A second home page view groups references by the kind of page they apply to.
Every home page description shortened to seven words or fewer.
UX Guidelines launches in six languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, and Chinese.
Glossary, People, By Year, and Site Map pages, plus bookmarks, sharing, and a share image for every page in every language.
